summary: A humorous local-news style piece on endangered species in the community, covering the threats of habitat destruction, invasive species, climate change and pollution. It quotes local experts on each threat and highlights conservation efforts such as wildlife corridors, breeding programs and the teen-led "Save Our Squeakers" program to reintroduce the Spotted Squeak Beetle. It closes with a hopeful, whimsical call for the community to keep its wildlife from disappearing.
one_line: A whimsical article on local endangered species, their threats (habitat loss, invasives, climate, pollution), and community conservation efforts like Save Our Squeakers.
key_facts: The Spotted Squeak Beetle, native to Greenleaf Forest, is endangered; reports dated September 5, 2023 indicate its numbers are very low.
Local herpetologist Dr. Amanda Hugginkiss says the habitats of the Half-Shelled Hurry-Up Turtles are shrinking because of urban development projects since September 2023.
Dr. Hugginkiss described a turtle returning to find a strip mall with a 'No Turtles Allowed' sign where a swamp used to be.
Invasive species expert Mr. Roger McSnootypants stated on October 12, 2023 that the Voracious Vermin, which arrived at the local docks, are eating native insects.
The Voracious Vermin are an invasive species described as coming from Vaguely-Victorian-England.
Climatologist Ms. Flora Fauna said last Tuesday, "It's hotter than a billy goat in a pepper patch," referring to global warming's effect on local species.
Pollution of air, water and soil has gone on for decades; the Confused Carp are cited as affected by toxic water.
Conservationist Barry Barrel warned that if the community doesn't clean up, fish may start growing limbs and walking out of the rivers in protest.
Conservation initiatives include wildlife corridors and breeding programs for critically lonely species.
"Save Our Squeakers" is led by local teen activist "Squeaky" Pete McGee, starting November 3, 2023.
Pete McGee's group, the "Squeak Squaders", reintroduces the Spotted Squeak Beetle into habitats that don't resemble a barren moonscape.
The article ends on a hopeful note that the community has the potential and determination to keep its wildlife from needing a farewell party.
